node:uv-coordinates.title: UV Coords
node:uv-coordinates.tagline: Gives you the position of each pixel as a vec2 (0–1), so you can drive patterns and effects from screen position.
node:uv-coordinates.hook: Connect out → Noise → Output to see a grayscale pattern on screen.
node:uv-coordinates.description: Outputs screen position as a vec2 from 0 to 1 in x and y. Connect out to Noise, Displace, or Transform to drive patterns from where each pixel sits on screen.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Position on screen (0–1 in x and y). Connect to Noise, Translate, Scale, or any node that takes vec2 coordinates.

examples: Connect to Noise, then Output to see a grayscale pattern (floats promote to vec3).
Feed into Translate or Scale to shift or zoom patterns.
Use with Polar Coords or Hex Grid for radial or tiled effects.
node:uv-coordinates.advanced: UV is normalized (0–1); bottom-left is (0, 0), top-right is (1, 1). Use Fragment Coords when you need pixel coordinates or aspect-ratio corrections; use Resolution with Divide for that.

node:time.title: Time
node:time.tagline: A number that keeps increasing over time—use it to animate motion, waves, or any value that should change as the shader runs.
node:time.hook: Connect out → Sine → Output for a smooth animated wave.
node:time.description: Outputs a float that increases every frame. Multiply it to speed up or slow down motion, or feed Sine/Cosine for smooth waves. No inputs or parameters—it always gives current shader time.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Current time in seconds. Connect to Sine, Cosine, Multiply, or Noise to drive animation.

examples: Connect to Sine or Cosine, then Output for a moving wave (floats promote to vec3).
Multiply Time by a small float to slow down (or large to speed up) animation.
Feed into Noise Time input for animated noise, or into Translate for moving patterns.

node:mixed-wave-signal.title: Mixed Wave
node:mixed-wave-signal.tagline: Three weighted sine or cosine waves combined into one float—organic motion without extra wiring.
node:mixed-wave-signal.description: Uses shader time internally (you do not need a separate Time node). Global speed and offset scale the phase for all waves. Each wave has its own speed, phase offset, weight, and whether it uses sine or cosine (0 = sine, 1 = cosine).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Remapped signal. Typical range follows Out min / Out max; use with Multiply, Mix, or drive animated parameters.

parameters.name: Global speed
parameters.description: Higher = faster motion or tighter repetition; zero often freezes animation.

parameters.name: Global offset
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

parameters.name: Out min
parameters.description: Adjusts Out min between -1 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Out max
parameters.description: Adjusts Out max between -1 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: Higher = faster motion or tighter repetition; zero often freezes animation.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

parameters.name: Weight
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

parameters.name: Shape
parameters.description: Switches the visual style or algorithm variant.

examples: Tune Wave 2/3 speeds slightly off 1.0 to get quasi-periodic, non-repeating motion.
Set Cosine to 1 on one wave for a 90° phase shift vs sine-only waves.
Use Out min / Out max to bias motion (e.g. 0 to 0.5) before Multiply into a parameter.
node:mixed-wave-signal.advanced: The three contributions are blended by weight and normalized so the mix stays in the −1 to 1 range, then mapped linearly to Out min and Out max (both between −1 and 1). Connect the output to parameters (via automation), math nodes, or Output for grayscale preview.

node:oscillator-2d.title: Oscillator 2D
node:oscillator-2d.tagline: Stacked sine motion on X and Y with rotation and offset—drive paired float parameters without hand-wiring LFOs.
node:oscillator-2d.description: Dual-axis LFO built from three sine layers per axis, optional rotation, then offset. Uses shader time—no separate Time node. Connect x and y to distortion centers (Vortex, Radial UV Warp) or any float pair.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: Horizontal oscillator value after stacks, rotation and offset.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: Vertical oscillator value after stacks, rotation and offset.

examples: Wire Oscillator X and Y into Vortex center X/Y; keep small amplitudes and layer three slightly different frequencies.
Set Rotation speed to spin the oscillator vector together; Rot wobble amplitude modulates spin rate subtly.
Use Offset to park the wandering path near a baseline while the stacks move around it.
On the target parameter, multiply mode combines the oscillator with the pad slider for proportional motion.
node:oscillator-2d.advanced: Layer mix (same for X and Y) chooses how partials combine: Sum (additive); Normalized (scaled sum to reduce blow-up when many layers are loud); Product (multiplies enabled amp×sin terms); Max absolute value (loudest enabled partial). Each layer has On, Amp, Freq, and Phase. Rotation uses Speed, Phase, and wobble controls. Outputs rotate in the XY plane, then Offset X/Y is added last.
node:oscillator-2d.hook: Wire x/y into Vortex center X/Y or Radial UV Warp offsets for wandering distortion.

parameters.name: Global speed
parameters.description: Higher = faster motion or tighter repetition; zero often freezes animation.

parameters.name: Global offset
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

parameters.name: Layer mix
parameters.description: More layers add detail or complexity; fewer stay simpler and faster.

parameters.name: On
parameters.description: Turns this section of the effect on or off.

parameters.name: Amp
parameters.description: Adjusts Amp between -5 and 5; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Freq
parameters.description: Adjusts Freq between -20 and 20; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: Higher = faster motion or tighter repetition; zero often freezes animation.

parameters.name: Wobble
parameters.description: Adjusts Wobble between -6.283 and 6.283; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Wob freq
parameters.description: Adjusts Wob freq between -20 and 20; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Wob phase
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

node:path-drive.title: Path Drive
node:path-drive.tagline: Preset XY paths (orbit, drift, pulse) with slow wander and fast jitter on one node.
node:path-drive.description: Uses shader time (no separate Time node). Pick a Path preset, then Size, Speed, and Phase set how far, how fast, and where the cycle starts along the curve. Center X/Y is the pivot; Wander and Jitter add slow and fast deviation.

outputs.name: x
outputs.description: Horizontal path position plus center, wander, and jitter.

outputs.name: y
outputs.description: Vertical path position plus center, wander, and jitter.

examples: Orbit + Aspect 1 + Size 0.2–0.4: circular bulge center motion; lower Aspect for a wider ellipse; raise Wander slightly for organic drift.
Figure-8 with Aspect ≠ 1: set Rotate to tilt the loop, or add a little Spin so the shape slowly turns and reads less static over time.
Drift preset for non-repeating roam; Jitter for subtle fast flicker on top.
Pulse preset with Pulse depth ~0.5: center stays on a circle while the path radius breathes.
One Path Drive per Radial UV Warp when stacking multiple distortions with different motion.
node:path-drive.advanced: Rotation (Rotate, Spin, Phase) turns the whole path—including wander and jitter—around Center; use this to tilt elliptical presets or slowly spin the motion for more variation with Aspect. Path Phase advances along the preset; it is not the same as spatial rotation. Orbit and Figure-8 expose Aspect (1 = circle on Orbit); Pulse depth for Pulse; Angle for Line. Outputs X and Y as separate floats—wire each to a center parameter on Radial UV Warp, Vortex, Ripple, and similar nodes. Use one Path Drive per distortion when you want independent motion. On the target parameter, input mode (override, add, multiply, …) controls how the driven value combines with the pad.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Whole-number control for Path. Higher values usually increase count or steps.

parameters.name: Center X
parameters.description: Moves the focal point across the canvas in normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: Center Y
parameters.description: Moves the focal point across the canvas in normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: Larger values enlarge the feature; smaller values make it finer or tighter.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: Higher = faster motion or tighter repetition; zero often freezes animation.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

parameters.name: Aspect
parameters.description: Adjusts Aspect between 0.2 and 4; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Wander
parameters.description: Adjusts Wander between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Jitter
parameters.description: Adjusts Jitter between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Rotate
parameters.description: Adjusts Rotate between 0 and 360; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Spin
parameters.description: Adjusts Spin between -5 and 5; higher values usually intensify the look.

node:resolution.title: Resolution
node:resolution.tagline: Use this to access screen resolution for aspect ratio calculations and pixel-perfect effects
node:resolution.description: Outputs the screen resolution as a vec2 containing the width and height in pixels. This is essential for maintaining aspect ratios, calculating pixel sizes, and creating resolution-independent effects. The x component represents width, and the y component represents height.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Screen resolution as (width, height) in pixels. Connect to Divide with Fragment Coords for aspect-correct coords, or to Bayer Dither and similar effects.

examples: Divide Fragment Coords by Resolution to get normalized 0–1 coords that respect aspect ratio.
Use with UV or Polar Coords to scale or dither in pixel space.
Feed width/height into Bayer Dither or other pixel-aware effects for consistent look at any resolution.
node:resolution.advanced: Connect Fragment Coords to Divide (a) and Resolution to Divide (b) for aspect-correct UV; or feed Resolution into UV or Polar Coords for pixel-aware effects. Resolution is in pixels (x = width, y = height). For aspect-correct UV, use Fragment Coords divided by Resolution; for simple 0–1 space use UV Coords.

node:fragment-coordinates.title: Frag Coords
node:fragment-coordinates.tagline: Frag Coords: Outputs the fragment coordinates (gl_FragCoord.xy)
node:fragment-coordinates.description: Outputs the fragment coordinates (gl_FragCoord.xy) as a vec2, representing the actual pixel position on the screen. Unlike UV coordinates which are normalized, fragment coordinates are in actual pixel units, with (0,0) at the bottom-left corner.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Fragment coordinates in pixel units (x, y). Connect to Divide (a) with Resolution (b) for normalized coords, or to pixel-based effects like Bayer Dither.

examples: Divide by Resolution for aspect-correct 0–1 coordinates; connect to Noise or Translate for pixel-aligned effects.
Use for Bayer Dither or Polar Coords when you need actual pixel position.
Feed into nodes that expect pixel units (e.g. precise positioning or resolution-dependent patterns).
node:fragment-coordinates.advanced: This is useful for pixel-perfect effects, precise positioning, and calculations that require actual screen dimensions. Connect to Divide with Resolution for aspect-correct 0–1 coords, or feed into Translate, Bayer Dither, or Polar Coords for pixel-aware effects. Fragment coords are in pixel space (bottom-left origin). Use when you need real pixel position or aspect ratio; use UV Coords when 0–1 normalized space is enough.

node:orbit-camera.title: Orbit Camera
node:orbit-camera.tagline: Camera orbiting a target — feeds ro/rd into 3D SDF / raymarch nodes
node:orbit-camera.description: Outputs ray origin (ro) and ray direction (rd) from a camera that orbits a target, driven by time. Connect Screen position (e.g.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Screen position for per-pixel ray direction. Should be connected — UV Coords or Fragment Coordinates work; without a connection rays don't vary per pixel and the result is a single dot.

outputs.name: ro
outputs.description: Ray origin (camera position on the orbit)

outputs.name: rd
outputs.description: Ray direction (normalized, per fragment when Screen position is connected)

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Orbit distance from the target — larger values pull the camera back. Combine with Target X/Y/Z to frame the scene.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: Orbit angular speed in radians per second. Negative reverses the spin; 0 freezes the camera (Phase still controls where it sits).

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Start-angle offset in degrees. Use to offset two cameras orbiting the same target, or to park a frozen camera (Speed = 0) at a specific azimuth.

parameters.name: Target X
parameters.description: World X of the look-at target the camera orbits around.

parameters.name: Target Y
parameters.description: World Y of the look-at target.

parameters.name: Target Z
parameters.description: World Z of the look-at target.

parameters.name: Tilt (rad)
parameters.description: Inclination in radians (±π/2 ≈ ±1.57). 0 keeps the camera level on the XZ plane; positive tilts it up over the target. Approaching ±π/2 pushes the camera near the world-up basis and rays can become unstable — back off slightly if you see glitchy directions.

parameters.name: FOV
parameters.description: Screen-spread multiplier applied to the per-pixel offset (1.0 is neutral). Larger widens the field; smaller narrows it. This is the inverse sense of Look-at Camera's Zoom (which is an image-plane distance) — both shape framing, but FOV grows wider as you turn it up while Zoom grows tighter.

examples: Connect UV Coords → in, then ro/rd into an SDF or raymarch node for an orbiting 3D view.
Set Speed to 0 and use Phase to park the camera at a specific azimuth for a still render.
Use a negative Speed (and matching Phase offset) on a second Orbit Camera to make two objects counter-orbit the same target.
node:orbit-camera.advanced: from UV Coords) so each pixel gets the correct ray direction; without it every pixel shoots the same forward ray and the connected SDF (signed distance field) collapses to a single dot. Speed can be negative to reverse the orbit, and Phase offsets the start angle so two cameras can orbit the same target out of sync. Connect ro and rd to nodes that expose ro/rd inputs (Box / Torus SDF, SDF Raymarch, Bokeh Point, …) to share this camera. Orbit moves the camera around a target over time; use Look-at Camera when you want a fixed camera position and explicit forward direction. The orbit basis uses world up (0,1,0); near ±π/2 Tilt the camera approaches that axis and the right/up vectors degenerate — keep Tilt a touch under the limit if rays glitch. FOV here is a screen-spread multiplier (higher = wider) and is the inverse sense of Look-at Camera's Zoom (higher = narrower); both shape framing, just with opposite knob direction.

node:look-at-camera.title: Look-at Camera
node:look-at-camera.tagline: Ray origin and direction from a fixed camera looking at a target (no orbit)
node:look-at-camera.description: Outputs ray origin (ro) and ray direction (rd) from a fixed camera position looking at a target. Use for drive-style or fixed-view 3D (e.g. bokeh lights, raymarching). Connect Screen position (e.g. UV Coords, or UV minus rain offset) for perspective.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Screen position for per-pixel ray direction (e.g. UV or normalized device coords)

outputs.name: ro
outputs.description: Ray origin (camera position)

outputs.name: rd
outputs.description: Ray direction (normalized, per fragment when Screen position is connected)

parameters.name: Position X
parameters.description: Camera world X. Together with Position Y/Z, sets ray origin before look direction is built.

parameters.name: Position Y
parameters.description: Moves the focal point across the canvas in normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: Position Z
parameters.description: Moves the focal point across the canvas in normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: Look-at target X
parameters.description: World X of the point the camera looks toward; forward is normalized from Position to this target.

parameters.name: Look-at target Y
parameters.description: World Y of the look-at point.

parameters.name: Look-at target Z
parameters.description: World Z of the look-at point.

parameters.name: Zoom
parameters.description: Distance along the view axis from the camera to the plane where Screen position spreads into ray offsets. Larger values push that plane farther forward (typically narrower / more telephoto); smaller pulls it closer (wider cone). This is not magnify-style zoom—compare with Orbit Camera’s FOV control.

examples: Connect UV to in; connect ro and rd to an SDF or Bokeh node for 3D raymarching.
Use with Rain Drops: subtract rain UV offset from UV, then feed into Look-at Camera for windshield effect.
Often used with Bokeh Point or Drive Home Lights for drive-style scenes.
node:look-at-camera.advanced: Position is the camera; Look-at target is the point it faces. Zoom moves the imaging plane forward along the view (focal-plane style distance): larger values usually feel more telephoto (narrower spread), smaller values wider; it is not magnify-style optical zoom. Look-at keeps the camera fixed; use Orbit Camera when you want the camera to move around a target over time. Basis construction uses world up (0,1,0); when the camera’s forward direction is nearly parallel to that axis, rays can become unstable or degenerate—tilt Position or Look-at target slightly if you see glitchy directions. Larger Zoom moves the imaging plane farther along forward (usually a tighter field); combine it with Position and Look-at target for framing rather than expecting magnify-style optical zoom.

node:rain-drops.title: Rain Drops
node:rain-drops.tagline: Procedural rain-on-glass UV offset for windshield distortion
node:rain-drops.description: Outputs a vec2 UV offset for rain drops on glass. Subtract from UV and feed to Look-at Camera for windshield distortion. Parameters: scale, seed, speed, layers, drop size variation, quantity per layer. Reference: Shadertoy The Drive Home.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV coordinates

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Time for animation (default: internal time)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: UV offset to subtract before camera (uv - out → camera)

examples: Feed UV into in and subtract the output from UV before connecting to Look-at Camera for windshield rain distortion.
Connect Time to the time input to animate drops; tune scale and quantity for density.
Use with Drive Home Lights: same UV pipeline (UV − rain offset → camera) for a rainy drive scene.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Larger values enlarge the feature; smaller values make it finer or tighter.

parameters.name: Seed
parameters.description: Changes the random layout; same seed gives the same pattern each run.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: Higher = faster motion or tighter repetition; zero often freezes animation.

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: More layers add detail or complexity; fewer stay simpler and faster.

parameters.name: Size var.
parameters.description: Larger values enlarge the feature; smaller values make it finer or tighter.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

node:bokeh-point.title: Bokeh Point
node:bokeh-point.tagline: Soft bokeh disc intensity for one 3D point light
node:bokeh-point.description: Outputs 0–1 intensity for a single 3D point as seen from a ray (ro, rd). Size is the world-space band from closest ray–point approach: smaller values need a tighter pass to light up; Blur only softens the outer edge. Multiply the output by light color.

inputs.name: ro
inputs.description: Ray origin. Connect ro from Look-at Camera or Orbit Camera.

inputs.name: rd
inputs.description: Ray direction. Connect rd from the same camera as ro.

inputs.name: point
inputs.description: Light position in 3D. Connect Constant Vec3 or any vec3 world-space position.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Disc intensity 0–1 (not the Blur parameter). Connect to Multiply with a color, Output, Mix, or toward Final Output.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: World-space crossing band: based on the shortest distance from the ray line to the point (perpendicular distance). Larger values light up from farther passes; very small values need an almost direct hit.

parameters.name: Blur
parameters.description: Edge softness of the disc (smoothstep range). Higher values spread the falloff over a wider distance band at the rim; does not change the peak center value.

parameters.name: Inner falloff
parameters.description: When on, slightly darkens the center of the disc relative to the rim for a less flat highlight. When off, the core stays brighter and more uniform.

examples: Connect Look-at or Orbit Camera ro/rd, and a Constant Vec3 as the light position; multiply output by a color and add to your scene.
Use several Bokeh Point nodes with different positions and colors for multiple lights.
Feed the float output into Output or Multiply with a color, then add to Final Output or mix with background.
node:bokeh-point.advanced: Inner falloff optionally darkens the disc center for a less flat core. Reference: Shadertoy The Drive Home.

node:bokeh.title: Bokeh
node:bokeh.tagline: Fullscreen post bokeh: iris highlights (WebGPU multipass before Final Output; inline stub when blended upstream)
node:bokeh.description: Post-process bokeh on a vec4 color chain—not the same as Bokeh Point (3D disc on a ray). On WebGPU, … → Bokeh → Final Output runs a multipass bright pass plus shaped blur; wiring upstream uses a lighter single-pass preview.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Scene or graded color. Typical chain: … → Bokeh → Final Output.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Combined color with bokeh highlights baked in (alpha preserved where supported).

examples: Chain Output → Bokeh → Final Output when WebGPU builds the multipass iris blur.
Compare with Bokeh Point when you want a literal 3D light disc from ro/rd, not a 2D post bloom.
Raise Threshold then Intensity/Strength/Radius until only bright regions bloom; tune Blades + Rotation on WebGPU for aperture shape.
node:bokeh.advanced: WebGL always uses a lightweight luminance plus angular iris modulation. Place before Final Output for full multipass quality on WebGPU, or upstream in a color chain for a quick inline effect.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: Higher keeps only stronger regions; lower includes more of the input.

parameters.name: Intensity
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Larger values enlarge the feature; smaller values make it finer or tighter.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

parameters.name: Blades
parameters.description: Whole-number control for Blades. Higher values usually increase count or steps.

parameters.name: Rotation
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

node:drive-home-lights.title: Drive Home Lights
node:drive-home-lights.tagline: Bokeh street, head, tail, and environment lights in one node
node:drive-home-lights.description: Outputs additive light color (not a full lit scene): street lights, headlights, tail and brake lights, and environment lights as soft bokeh discs, plus a sky tint built from two OKLCH (perceptual lightness, chroma, hue) colors.

inputs.name: ro
inputs.description: Ray origin. Connect from Look-at Camera or Orbit Camera.

inputs.name: rd
inputs.description: Ray direction. Connect from the same camera as ro.

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Time for animation. Connect Time node for driving light motion.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Additive light color including built-in sky tint (two OKLCH stops + ray falloff) and strength

parameters.name: Sky low L
parameters.description: OKLCH lightness for the sky tint when the ray looks lower—pairs with the left swatch above.

parameters.name: Sky low C
parameters.description: OKLCH chroma for the low-elevation sky tint (left swatch). Higher is more saturated.

parameters.name: Sky low H
parameters.description: OKLCH hue (degrees) for the low-elevation sky tint (left swatch).

parameters.name: Sky high L
parameters.description: OKLCH lightness for the sky tint when the ray looks higher—pairs with the right swatch above.

parameters.name: Sky high C
parameters.description: OKLCH chroma for the high-elevation sky tint (right swatch).

parameters.name: Sky high H
parameters.description: OKLCH hue (degrees) for the high-elevation sky tint (right swatch).

parameters.name: Sky strength
parameters.description: Scales how strong the sky tint contribution is on top of the bokeh lights. Does not replace the horizon darkening—elevation still controls how much sky appears.

parameters.name: Time scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the connected time input before driving all motion (traffic, flicker, loops). Higher scrolls the drive faster.

parameters.name: Tail-light lanes
parameters.description: Biases how tail lights pick a lane side from procedural noise—higher values favor one pattern of left/right spacing; lower values favor the opposite. Adjust for variety, not overall road position.

examples: Connect ro/rd from Look-at Camera and Time; plug output into Final Output or add with a sky gradient.
Combine with Rain Drops: use (UV − rain offset) as the screen input to the same Look-at Camera for a rainy drive.

Use sky low/high to tint the visible sky (defaults match the classic single purple); darkness near the horizon comes from ray elevation, not a separate “black” color stop. Adjust sky strength, time scale, and Tail-light lanes to match the drive mood.
node:drive-home-lights.advanced: How much sky you see still follows ray elevation—looking toward the horizon stays darker; the low/high colors only tint the part of the sky that is already visible. Multiply or add with other colors as needed; combine with Look-at Camera (ro/rd) and Time. Reference: Shadertoy The Drive Home.

node:constant-float.title: Float
node:constant-float.tagline: A single number you set with a slider. Use it wherever another node needs a float (speed, strength, threshold, etc.).
node:constant-float.hook: Set Value, then connect out to Multiply or Mix to scale or blend downstream.
node:constant-float.description: One number you control with the Value knob. No inputs—set Value and connect out to Multiply (scale), Mix (blend weight), Displace, or any float port.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The number set by the Value parameter. Connect to Add, Multiply, Mix, Translate, Scale, or any float input.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The number this node outputs. Higher raises brightness or strength downstream; lower softens or slows the effect you feed (e.g. Multiply scale or Mix weight).

examples: Set Value and connect to Multiply to scale noise or animation speed; to Mix for blend amount; to Translate or Scale for offset.
Use as fallback when a float input is unconnected (e.g. Mix amount, Sine frequency).
Connect to Sine or Cosine for a fixed phase or frequency when you don't need Time.

node:constant-vec2.title: Vec2
node:constant-vec2.tagline: Vec2: Outputs a constant vec2 value
node:constant-vec2.description: Outputs a constant vec2 value with adjustable x and y components. This node is perfect for providing fixed 2D values such as coordinate offsets, scale factors, translation amounts, or any pair of related float values.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The constant vec2 value with (x, y) components. Connect to Translate, Scale, Distance, or any vec2 input.

examples: Set x, y, z and connect to Translate or Scale for 2D offset/scale; to Rotate for center; to UV-based nodes for fixed vec2.
Use as a constant offset to Add with UV or other vec2 for shifted patterns.
Feed into Noise, Hex Grid, or Wave Patterns as a fixed coordinate or scale input.
node:constant-vec2.advanced: Both x and y components can be independently adjusted between -1000.0 and 1000.0. Connect to Translate or Scale for offsets, to Distance (a or b) for a center point, or to Noise and other nodes that take vec2.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

node:constant-vec3.title: Vec3
node:constant-vec3.tagline: Vec3: Outputs a constant vec3 value
node:constant-vec3.description: Outputs a constant vec3 value with adjustable x, y, and z components. This node is useful for providing fixed 3D values such as positions, direction vectors, RGB color values (before conversion to color nodes), or any triple of related float values.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The constant vec3 value with (x, y, z) components. Connect to Bokeh Point, camera nodes, or 3D shape/lighting inputs.

examples: Set (x, y, z) for RGB or position; connect to Output, Mix, Bokeh Point position, or Final Output for a solid color.
Use as light or object position in 3D (e.g. Bokeh Point point input) or as RGB for tinting.
Connect to OKLCH Color Map Bezier or other nodes that take vec3 color or position.
node:constant-vec3.advanced: All three components can be independently adjusted between -1000.0 and 1000.0. Connect to Bokeh Point (point), Look-at Camera (position/lookat), or any 3D node that expects a vec3.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

parameters.name: Z
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

node:constant-vec4.title: Vec4
node:constant-vec4.tagline: Use this to provide constant 4D vectors for RGBA colors, homogeneous coordinates, or 4D data
node:constant-vec4.description: Outputs a constant vec4 value with adjustable x, y, z, and w components. This node is essential for providing fixed 4D values such as RGBA color values, homogeneous coordinates for 3D transformations, or any quadruple of related float values.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The constant vec4 value with (x, y, z, w) components. Connect to Blend or any vec4 input.

node:constant-vec4.advanced: All four components can be independently adjusted between -1000.0 and 1000.0, with w defaulting to 1.0. Connect to Blend or other nodes that accept vec4 for color or homogeneous data.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

parameters.name: Z
parameters.description: Component offset along that axis; positive shifts right/up/forward depending on context.

parameters.name: W
parameters.description: Adjusts W between -1000 and 1000; higher values usually intensify the look.

examples: Wire Vec4 into nodes that expect its output type (see Inputs/Outputs above).
Pair with UV, Time, or Resolution for common fullscreen shader setups.

node:oklch-color.title: OKLCH Color
node:oklch-color.tagline: OKLCH Color: Defines an OKLCH color value
node:oklch-color.description: Defines a color value in the OKLCH (OK Lightness, Chroma, Hue) color space, which provides perceptually uniform color representation. This means that equal changes in the L, C, or H values result in visually similar changes in perceived color.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: OKLCH color value as (lightness, chroma, hue). Connect to OKLCH Color Map nodes for smooth gradients.

examples: Set L, C, H and connect to OKLCH Color Map Bezier or Output for a base color in a gradient.
Use with Mix or OKLCH Color Map Threshold for perceptually smooth color transitions.
Combine several OKLCH Color nodes in a gradient chain for smooth, uniform steps.
node:oklch-color.advanced: The node outputs a vec3 containing (L, C, H) values, where L (lightness) ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, C (chroma/saturation) ranges from 0.0 to 0.4, and H (hue) ranges from 0.0 to 360.0 degrees. This color space is particularly useful for smooth color gradients and color interpolation. Connect to OKLCH Color Map Bezier or OKLCH Color Map Threshold for perceptually smooth gradients from a single value. OKLCH is perceptually uniform: equal changes in L, C, or H look equally different to the eye, which makes gradients and interpolation smoother than in RGB.

parameters.name: Lightness
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

parameters.name: Chroma
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

parameters.name: Hue
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

node:bezier-curve.title: Bezier
node:bezier-curve.tagline: Bezier: Defines a cubic bezier curve for color interpolation
node:bezier-curve.description: Defines a cubic Bezier curve for smooth interpolation and easing functions. The node outputs a vec4 containing the two control points (x1, y1, x2, y2) that define the curve's shape.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Bezier curve control points as (x1, y1, x2, y2). Connect to OKLCH Color Map Bezier or other curve-based nodes.

examples: Connect to OKLCH Color Map Bezier as lCurve to shape how a value maps to color (ease-in, ease-out, custom).
Use with Mix for smooth blend curves or with Smoothstep for custom easing.
Drag control points in the editor to design the curve; the output vec4 drives the mapping in color or blend nodes.
node:bezier-curve.advanced: This curve can be used with color mapping nodes to create smooth color transitions, or with animation systems to define easing functions. The curve is visualized in a bezier editor interface where you can drag control points to adjust the curve shape. The curve maps input values (0-1) to output values (0-1) with customizable easing. Connect to OKLCH (perceptual lightness, chroma, hue) Color Map Bezier for smooth color ramps, or use with any node that accepts a curve definition. The curve maps 0–1 input to 0–1 output. Use it for easing (slow start/end) or for remapping values before color or blend; linear would be (0,0,1,1).

parameters.name: Start X
parameters.description: Adjusts Start X between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Start Y
parameters.description: Adjusts Start Y between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: End X
parameters.description: Adjusts End X between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: End Y
parameters.description: Adjusts End Y between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

node:add.title: Add
node:add.tagline: Adds two numbers (or two vec2/vec3/vec4 values). Use it to combine values or add an offset.
node:add.hook: Connect two signals to a and b, or leave b empty and set B for a fixed offset.
node:add.description: Outputs a + b. Leave b unconnected to use the B knob instead. Handy for shifting Time, combining two waves, or adding an offset before Output.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: A. Connect Time, Float, Sine, or another node’s output.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: B. If unconnected, the B parameter is used.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The sum a + b. Connect to Multiply, Mix, Translate, or other math/effect nodes.

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback when b is unconnected. Higher B lifts the sum (brighter on Output); negative B pulls it down. Use with Time on a to phase-shift animation.

examples: Connect Time to a and a constant to b (or B) to shift animation in time.
Add two Sine waves or two Noise outputs for combined patterns.
Use with Translate: add a vec2 offset to UV for shifting the whole pattern.

node:subtract.title: Subtract
node:subtract.tagline: Outputs a − b. Use for offsets, differences, and centering patterns around zero.
node:subtract.description: Subtracts b from a. Leave b unconnected to use the B knob. Handy for (UV − center), (Noise − 0.5), or any difference before Absolute or Length.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The value to subtract from. Often UV, Time, or a pattern output.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The value to subtract. Often a center point (Constant Vec2), threshold, or offset.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The difference a − b. Connect to Absolute, Length, Output, or Smoothstep for falloffs.

examples: Subtract a center from UV.x or UV.y before Length or Distance for radial effects.
Use (Noise − 0.5) to center a pattern around zero, then feed to Output.
Combine with Absolute to get a distance-like value from a difference.
node:subtract.hook: Connect UV to a and a center Vec2 to b, then Length or Smoothstep for radial falloff.

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback when b is unconnected. Higher B pulls the result down; lower B lifts it. Use to offset Time or UV without a second wire.

node:multiply.title: Multiply
node:multiply.tagline: Multiplies two numbers. Use it to scale a value (e.g. slow down or speed up time) or combine signals.
node:multiply.hook: Connect Time to a and a small Float to b—or leave b empty and tune B—to slow or speed animation.
node:multiply.description: Outputs a × b. Leave b unconnected to use the B knob. Connect Time to a and a small float to b to slow motion, or scale Sine/Noise strength before Output.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: A. Often Time, Sine, or a pattern node’s output.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: B. If unconnected, the B parameter is used.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The product a × b. Connect to Add, Mix, Sine input, or Final Output (floats promote to vec3).

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback when b is unconnected. Below 1 dampens the result (dimmer/slower); above 1 amplifies it (brighter/faster). Zero flattens to black on Output.

examples: Connect Time to a and a small constant to b (or B) to slow down animation.
Multiply Sine by a float to change wave strength before Output.
Scale a Noise or Distance value before feeding into Smoothstep or Output.

node:divide.title: Divide
node:divide.tagline: Outputs a ÷ b. Use to normalize values or compute ratios (avoid dividing by zero).
node:divide.description: Divides a by b. Leave b unconnected to use the B knob. Watch for zero divisors—use a small constant or Clamp on b when needed.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The dividend (value to be divided). Often Fragment Coords, Distance, or Length.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The divisor (value to divide by). Often Resolution or a constant for normalization.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The quotient. Connect to Output, Multiply, or UV-style inputs for normalized values.

node:divide.hook: Connect Fragment Coords to a and Resolution to b for aspect-correct normalized coords.

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback when b is unconnected. Larger B shrinks the quotient; smaller B amplifies it. Set near 1 for gentle scaling.

examples: Fragment Coords ÷ Resolution for normalized screen coords.
Distance ÷ radius for normalized falloff before Smoothstep or Output.
Invert a scale: connect 1 (or a constant) to a and your scale to b.

node:power.title: Power
node:power.tagline: Raises base to an exponent. Use for gamma curves and non-linear remapping.
node:power.description: Outputs base^exponent. Leave exponent unconnected to use the Exponent knob. Fractional exponents give roots (0.5 ≈ square root).

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The base value to raise to a power. Often Smoothstep, Noise, or UV-derived value.

inputs.name: exponent
inputs.description: The exponent to raise the base to. Use a constant (e.g. 2, 0.5) or connect a float.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The result. Connect to Output, Mix, or Clamp for non-linear remapping.

examples: Raise Smoothstep or Noise to an exponent for gamma-like falloff curves.
Use base from UV or pattern and exponent 2 for quadratic falloff.
Power of 0.5 is equivalent to Square Root for non-linear remapping.
node:power.advanced: Fractional exponents give roots (e.g. 0.5 = square root). For e^x use Exponential; for arbitrary base use Power.
node:power.hook: Connect Smoothstep or Noise to base and a constant exponent (e.g. 2 or 0.5) for curved falloff.

parameters.name: Exponent
parameters.description: Fallback when exponent is unconnected. Above 1 steepens bright regions; below 1 softens; 2 squares the input for quadratic curves.

node:square-root.title: Square Root
node:square-root.tagline: Use this to calculate square roots and normalize distances
node:square-root.description: Calculates the square root of the input value. Commonly used for distance calculations, normalizing magnitudes, and creating smooth falloff curves. The square root is equivalent to raising a value to the power of 0.5. Connect Length or Distance output to in, then to Smoothstep or Output for soft falloff; or use after Dot Product for magnitude.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to calculate the square root of. Often Length, Distance, or Dot Product output.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The square root. Connect to Smoothstep, Mix, or Output for soft falloff.

examples: Feed Length or dot-product result into Square Root for magnitude before Smoothstep.
Use after Distance for softer falloff in radial gradients.
Normalize a squared value (e.g. from Dot Product) back to a length.

node:absolute.title: Absolute
node:absolute.tagline: Perfect for removing negative values and calculating magnitudes
node:absolute.description: Returns the absolute value of the input, removing any negative sign. Useful for distance calculations, ensuring positive values, and working with differences where direction doesn't matter. Connect (UV − 0.5) or (Noise − threshold) to get magnitude for falloff; feed Subtract output here when direction does not matter.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value. Often Subtract output, Sine, or Noise for magnitude-only use.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The absolute value (always positive or zero). Connect to Multiply, Mix, or Output.

examples: Use on (UV − 0.5) or (Noise − threshold) to get magnitude for falloff.
Feed Subtract output into Absolute when direction does not matter.
Combine with Distance for symmetric masks around a point.

node:floor.title: Floor
node:floor.tagline: Ideal for rounding down to the nearest integer
node:floor.description: Rounds the input value down to the nearest integer. Useful for creating discrete steps, grid-based effects, and quantizing values. Always rounds towards negative infinity. Connect UV × scale or Time to in for discrete cells or frame steps; use with Modulo for repeating tile indices in grids.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to round down. Often UV × scale, Time, or Multiply output.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The largest integer less than or equal to the input. Connect to Modulo, Output, or grid nodes.

examples: Floor(UV × scale) or Floor(Time) for discrete cells or frame steps.
Use with Modulo for repeating tile indices in grids.
Quantize a value before Output for stepped gradients.

node:ceil.title: Ceil
node:ceil.tagline: Rounds up to the nearest integer. Use for ceiling division and discrete steps.
node:ceil.description: Rounds in up toward positive infinity. Pair with Floor or Fract for grid and tiling math.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to round up. Often Multiply, Divide, or UV-derived value.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The smallest integer ≥ input. Connect to Add, Multiply, Modulo, or grid nodes.

node:ceil.hook: Connect Multiply(UV, scale) to in for tile indices, then Modulo or a grid node.
examples: Ceil(UV × scale) for cell indices in repeating grids.
Ceil(Time) for whole-second or frame-step counters.
Use after Divide when you need ceiling division.

node:fract.title: Fract
node:fract.tagline: Keeps the fractional part (0–1). Essential for tiling and repeating patterns.
node:fract.description: Returns the decimal part of in, always between 0 and 1. Same idea as Modulo by 1—great for repeating UV or animation cycles.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value. Often UV × scale, Time, or Distance for repeating 0–1.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The fractional part (0–1). Connect to Smoothstep, Rings, Output, or grid nodes.

node:fract.hook: Connect UV × scale or Time to in, then Smoothstep or Rings for tiled bands.
examples: Fract(UV × 8) for eight repeating cells across the canvas.
Fract(Time) for a looping 0–1 phase driver into Sine.
Feed output to Smoothstep for soft edges inside each tile.

node:modulo.title: Modulo
node:modulo.tagline: Remainder after division. Wraps values into a repeating range.
node:modulo.description: Outputs the remainder of a ÷ b. Leave b unconnected to use the B knob. Result stays between 0 and b.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The dividend. Often Time, UV, or Multiply for wrapping.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The divisor. Usually a constant (e.g. 1 for 0–1 wrap).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The remainder. Connect to Sine, Smoothstep, Rings, or Output for cycles.

node:modulo.hook: Connect Time or UV × scale to a and 1 to b for a looping 0–1 cycle.

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback divisor when b is unconnected. Set to 1 to wrap into 0–1; higher values widen the repeat period.

examples: Modulo(Time, 1) for a repeating animation phase.
Modulo(Floor(UV × n), n) for grid cell indices.
Wrap a growing value before Sine or Smoothstep for cyclic motion.

node:min.title: Min
node:min.tagline: Use this to find the smaller of two values
node:min.description: Returns the minimum (smaller) of two input values. Useful for clamping values from above, finding the lower bound, and implementing conditional logic based on value comparisons. Connect a signal (e.g. Noise, distance) to a and an upper limit to b, then output to Output or Mix; often used with Max for soft clamping.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: A — value to compare

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: B — value to compare

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The smaller of the two input values

examples: Min(Noise, 1.0) or Min(distance, radius) to cap from above.
Combine two signals and take the smaller for darken-style blending.
Limit a value before feeding to Mix or Output.

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback when b is unconnected. Sets the comparison floor; output never exceeds a but can drop with B.

node:max.title: Max
node:max.tagline: Perfect for finding the larger of two values
node:max.description: Returns the maximum (larger) of two input values. Useful for clamping values from below, finding the upper bound, and implementing conditional logic based on value comparisons. Connect a signal to a and a lower limit to b, then to Output or Mix; often used with Min for clamping to a range.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: A — value to compare

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: B — value to compare

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The larger of the two input values

examples: Max(Noise, 0.0) or Max(distance − radius, 0) to clamp from below.
Combine two signals and take the larger for lighten-style blending.
Ensure a value is above a threshold before Smoothstep or Mix.

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback when b is unconnected. Sets the comparison ceiling; output never falls below B when a is lower.

node:clamp.title: Clamp
node:clamp.tagline: Keeps a value between min and max. Use to hold signals in a safe range.
node:clamp.description: Returns in clamped between min and max. Unconnected min/max use the Minimum and Maximum knobs. Keeps wild signals in 0–1 for Mix or Output.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to clamp

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: The minimum allowed value

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: The maximum allowed value

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The clamped value (between min and max)

node:clamp.hook: Connect Noise or Sine to in and set min/max (or wire Float constants) before Output.

parameters.name: Minimum
parameters.description: Fallback lower bound when min is unconnected. Values below this show as the floor on Output.

parameters.name: Maximum
parameters.description: Fallback upper bound when max is unconnected. Values above this cap at the ceiling on Output.

examples: Clamp(Sine, 0, 1) to map a wave into a 0–1 mask.
Clamp(Distance, 0, radius) for a radial cap before Smoothstep.
Hold Noise or Add output in 0–1 before Color Map or Mix.
node:clamp.advanced: For quick 0–1 clamping without extra ports, see Saturate or Clamp 0–1 in Utilities.

node:mix.title: Mix
node:mix.tagline: Blends two values by a factor: 0 = first, 1 = second. Use for crossfades, masks, and smooth transitions.
node:mix.hook: Wire two patterns to a and b, then drive Mix toward 0 or 1 to crossfade on Output.
node:mix.description: Blends a and b by the Mix weight: 0 returns a, 1 returns b, values in between crossfade. Connect two Noise or Sine outputs and a 0–1 driver (Smoothstep, UV.x, or the Mix knob) to t.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first value (returned when t = 0.0)

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second value (returned when t = 1.0)

inputs.name: t
inputs.description: Interpolation weight (shown as Mix on the node; typically 0.0 to 1.0)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The interpolated value between a and b

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Fallback when a is unconnected. Sets the low end of the blend; at Mix 0 you see this value on Output.

parameters.name: B
parameters.description: Fallback when b is unconnected. Sets the high end; at Mix 1 you see this value on Output.

parameters.name: Mix
parameters.description: Blend weight when t is unconnected. 0 shows only a; 1 shows only b; 0.5 is an even crossfade. Drag toward 1 to reveal b.

examples: Connect two Noise (or Sine) outputs to a and b, and Smoothstep to t for a blended mask.
Crossfade two patterns: one to a, one to b, and a 0–1 factor to t.
Mix two float sources and wire the result to Output (floats promote to vec3).

node:step.title: Step
node:step.tagline: Use this to create hard thresholds and binary decisions
node:step.description: Returns 0.0 if the input value is less than the edge value, otherwise returns 1.0. Creates a hard step function that's useful for creating binary masks, thresholds, and on/off switches based on value comparisons.

inputs.name: edge
inputs.description: The threshold value to compare against

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The value to compare with the edge

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: 0.0 if x < edge, 1.0 otherwise

examples: Step(threshold, Noise) for a hard cut between two regions.
Create a binary mask from Distance or Length for sharp edges.
Use output as condition for Select or as mask for Mix.
node:step.advanced: Step gives a hard 0/1 boundary; use Smoothstep when you want a smooth transition between two edges.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: Fallback edge when edge is unconnected. Output jumps from 0 to 1 when x crosses this value.

node:smoothstep.title: Smoothstep
node:smoothstep.tagline: Smooth 0–1 ramp between two edges. Softer than Step for fades and masks.
node:smoothstep.description: Returns 0 below edge0, 1 above edge1, and a smooth S-curve between. Unconnected edges use the Lower Edge and Upper Edge knobs.

inputs.name: edge0
inputs.description: The lower edge of the transition (returns 0.0 below this)

inputs.name: edge1
inputs.description: The upper edge of the transition (returns 1.0 above this)

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The input value to evaluate

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Smoothly interpolated value between 0.0 and 1.0

node:smoothstep.hook: Connect Distance or UV.x to x and set Lower/Upper Edge for a soft radial or horizontal fade.

parameters.name: Lower Edge
parameters.description: Fallback start of the ramp when edge0 is unconnected. Output stays 0 until x passes this value.

parameters.name: Upper Edge
parameters.description: Fallback end of the ramp when edge1 is unconnected. Output reaches 1 at and above this value.

examples: Smoothstep(0.2, 0.8, UV.x) for a horizontal vignette fade.
Smoothstep(inner, outer, Distance) for soft radial rings.
Drive Mix t from Smoothstep for eased crossfades instead of linear.
node:smoothstep.advanced: Step gives a hard 0/1 cut at one threshold; Smoothstep eases between two edges.

node:sine.title: Sine
node:sine.tagline: Oscillates between −1 and 1. Drive with Time or UV for waves.
node:sine.description: Sine of the input angle in radians. Feeds stripes, displacement, and any periodic motion when driven by Time or coordinates.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The angle in radians

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The sine value (between -1.0 and 1.0)

node:sine.hook: Connect Time (or UV × scale) to in and wire out to Output or Displace for motion.
examples: Time → Sine → Output for a pulsing brightness wave.
Sine(UV.x × 10) for vertical stripes; multiply amplitude before Output.
Add two Sine nodes (different phases) for richer interference patterns.

node:cosine.title: Cosine
node:cosine.tagline: Oscillates like Sine but phase-shifted 90°. Pair with Sine for circles.
node:cosine.description: Cosine of the input angle in radians. Same −1 to 1 range as Sine; offset phase makes it useful for rotations and paired waves.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The angle in radians

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The cosine value (between -1.0 and 1.0)

node:cosine.hook: Connect Time to in alongside Sine on the same driver for circular or Lissajous motion.
examples: Cosine(Time) + Sine(Time) on vec2 components for circular UV motion.
Cosine(UV.y × scale) for horizontal banding complementary to Sine on x.
Feed Transform or Displace with Cosine-driven offsets for orbital drift.

node:tangent.title: Tangent
node:tangent.tagline: Ideal for calculating slopes and ratios in trigonometry
node:tangent.description: Calculates the tangent of the input angle (in radians). The tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine. Returns values from negative to positive infinity, with discontinuities at odd multiples of π/2. Useful for advanced trigonometric calculations.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The angle in radians

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The tangent value

examples: Tangent(Time) for sharp periodic peaks (clamp input to avoid discontinuities).
Use with Arc Tangent for angle recovery from slope ratios.
Feed normalized angles for repeating saw-like or spike patterns.
node:tangent.advanced: Tangent has discontinuities at ±π/2; clamp input or use modulo to stay within a safe range. Prefer Sine/Cosine for smooth waves.

node:arc-sine.title: Arc Sine
node:arc-sine.tagline: Turns a sine value (−1 to 1) back into an angle in radians.
node:arc-sine.description: Inverse sine: input must stay in −1 to 1. Output angle spans −π/2 to π/2. Pairs with Sine for round-trip angle math.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The sine value (must be between -1.0 and 1.0)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The angle in radians (between -π/2 and π/2)

node:arc-sine.hook: Clamp or Mix a wave into −1…1, then Arc Sine → Multiply for angle-based rotation.
examples: Arc Sine(Sine(Time)) recovers the original phase (within range).
Map a normalized mask back to an angle before Transform rotation.
Clamp dot or mix output to −1…1 before Arc Sine.

node:arc-cosine.title: Arc Cosine
node:arc-cosine.tagline: Turns a cosine value (−1 to 1) back into an angle in radians.
node:arc-cosine.description: Inverse cosine: input in −1 to 1, output angle 0 to π. Use when you know cosine and need the angle.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The cosine value (must be between -1.0 and 1.0)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The angle in radians (between 0.0 and π)

node:arc-cosine.hook: Feed Dot Product or Cosine output (clamped) to recover an angle for rotation nodes.
examples: Arc Cosine(Cosine(phase)) for phase recovery on one quadrant.
Angle from a normalized direction dot product before Orient or Transform.
Pair with Arc Sine when splitting x/y angle components.

node:arc-tangent.title: Arc Tangent
node:arc-tangent.tagline: Converts a slope ratio to an angle (−π/2 to π/2).
node:arc-tangent.description: Inverse tangent of one value—covers two quadrants only. For full 360° from x and y, use Arc Tangent 2 instead.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The tangent value (ratio)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The angle in radians (between -π/2 and π/2)

node:arc-tangent.hook: Connect Divide(y, x) or Tangent output to get an angle from a ratio.
examples: Arc Tangent(Tangent(angle)) to recover angle from slope (within range).
Angle from a single ratio before driving Sine or rotation.
Use Arc Tangent 2 when you have separate x and y components.

node:arc-tangent-2.title: Arc Tangent 2
node:arc-tangent-2.tagline: Angle from (x, y) coords covering all four quadrants (−π to π).
node:arc-tangent-2.description: Returns atan2(y, x): direction from the x-axis to point (x, y). Leave x unconnected to use the X Component knob.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: The y-coordinate of the point

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The x-coordinate of the point

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The angle in radians (between -π and π)

node:arc-tangent-2.hook: Split UV or a vec2 into y and x, then Arc Tangent 2 → Sine/Cosine for polar motion.

parameters.name: X Component
parameters.description: Fallback x when the x port is unconnected. With y wired, sets the angle quadrant; zero x gives ±π/2.

examples: UV.y and UV.x (minus center) for a radial angle field.
Drive Kaleidoscope or Polar Coordinates from the angle output.
Angle → Sine/Cosine for orbiting displacement patterns.

node:exponential.title: Exponential
node:exponential.tagline: e raised to the input. Sharp growth above 0, decay below 0.
node:exponential.description: Outputs e^in. Positive inputs grow quickly; negative inputs decay toward zero. Inverse of Natural Logarithm.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The exponent to raise e to

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: e raised to the power of the input

node:exponential.hook: Connect a small negative Time × scale to in for fade-out curves; positive for bloom-like growth.
examples: Exponential(−Time × k) for smooth decay envelopes.
Contrast boost: Exponential on a 0–1 mask (keep input modest).
Pair with Natural Logarithm to compress large ranges.

node:natural-logarithm.title: Natural Logarithm
node:natural-logarithm.tagline: Log base e. Compresses large values; input must stay above zero.
node:natural-logarithm.description: Natural log of in; undefined at zero—keep input positive. Inverse of Exponential; useful for perceptual compression.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to calculate the logarithm of (must be > 0)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The natural logarithm of the input

node:natural-logarithm.hook: Connect Distance or Length (plus a tiny offset) to compress wide ranges before Mix.
examples: Log(Distance + ε) for softer falloff than linear distance.
Compress Exponential output back to a manageable range.
Audio-style dynamics: log on amplitude before remapping.

node:length.title: Length
node:length.tagline: Vector magnitude—distance from origin. Radial falloffs start here.
node:length.description: Length of the input vector. For vec2 UV centered at 0, this is distance from the middle of the canvas.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The vector. Often UV, Translate output, or position for radial falloff.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Magnitude (length). Connect to Smoothstep, Output, or Square Root for falloff.

node:length.hook: Connect UV (minus center via Subtract) to in, then Smoothstep or Output for a radial gradient.
examples: Length(UV − 0.5) for a circular vignette from center.
Length of a displacement vector before normalizing direction.
Feed Rings or Smoothstep for concentric banding.

node:distance.title: Distance
node:distance.tagline: Distance between two points. Core of radial masks and proximity effects.
node:distance.description: Euclidean distance from a to b. Leave b unwired to use Target X and Target Y knobs as a fixed second point.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first point. Often UV, Translate output, or center.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second point. Often Constant Vec2 (center) or another UV/position.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Distance between a and b. Connect to Smoothstep, Output, or Rings for radial effects.

node:distance.hook: Connect UV to a and Constant Vec2 (center) to b—or set Target X/Y—for a radial falloff.

parameters.name: Target X
parameters.description: Fallback x for point b when b is unconnected. Moves the falloff center horizontally on screen.

parameters.name: Target Y
parameters.description: Fallback y for point b when b is unconnected. Moves the falloff center vertically on screen.

examples: UV to a, (0.5, 0.5) to b → Smoothstep for a soft spotlight.
Animate b with Time-driven Vec2 for moving proximity masks.
Distance before Divide by radius for normalized ring widths.

node:dot-product.title: Dot Product
node:dot-product.tagline: Measures alignment of two vectors. Lighting and facing tests.
node:dot-product.description: Dot product of a and b. When both are unit vectors, result is cosine of the angle between them (−1 to 1).

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first vector. Often Normalize(UV) or a direction from a node.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second vector. Often Normalize output, Normal Mapping, or Constant Vec2.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Dot product (scalar). Connect to Lighting Shading, Mix, Smoothstep, or Output.

node:dot-product.hook: Normalize UV direction to a and a light direction to b, then Mix or Output for facing highlights.
examples: Normalize(UV) · light direction for simple directional shading.
Dot two pattern vectors for correlation-style masking.
Feed abs(dot) or Smoothstep(dot) for front-facing highlights.
node:dot-product.advanced: For unit inputs, dot equals cosine of the angle; multiply by lengths if vectors are not normalized.

node:cross-product.title: Cross Product
node:cross-product.tagline: Perpendicular vec3 from two 3D vectors. Surface normals and orientation.
node:cross-product.description: Cross product of vec3 a and b. Output is perpendicular to both; magnitude equals the parallelogram area.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first 3D vector. Often Normalize or Normal Mapping output.

inputs.name: b
inputs.description: The second 3D vector. Often Normalize or Normal Mapping output.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Cross product (perpendicular vector). Connect to Normalize, Normal Mapping, or Lighting Shading.

node:cross-product.hook: Cross two tangent directions, then Normalize, for a surface normal in 3D setups.
examples: Cross edge vectors on a 3D surface, then Normalize for normals.
Orientation test: sign of cross z tells which side is facing.
Feed Normal Mapping or Lighting Shading with the result.

node:normalize.title: Normalize
node:normalize.tagline: Unit vector (length 1) in the same direction. Direction without distance.
node:normalize.description: Divides the vector by its length. Output points the same way but with magnitude 1—use for directions and normals.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The vector to normalize. Often UV, Translate output, or polar/position vector.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Unit vector (length 1). Connect to Dot Product, Reflect, Refract, or Lighting Shading.

node:normalize.hook: Connect UV or a displacement vector to in, then Dot Product or Reflect for direction-only math.
examples: Normalize(UV − center) for outward radial directions.
Direction into Reflect or Refract for bounce effects.
Normalize before Dot Product so result equals cosine of angle.

node:reflect.title: Reflect
node:reflect.tagline: Bounces an incident vector off a surface normal.
node:reflect.description: Reflects incident vector I about normal N. Both should be directions; normalize inputs for predictable angles.

inputs.name: I
inputs.description: Incident direction. Often Normalize(UV) or view/light direction.

inputs.name: N
inputs.description: Surface normal (normalized). Often from Normal Mapping or Constant Vec2.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Reflected direction. Connect to Dot Product or Lighting Shading for specular.

node:reflect.hook: Wire Normalize(view dir) to I and Normalize(surface normal) to N for mirror-like bounce.
examples: Specular highlight: reflect view/light dir about the normal.
Mirror UV warp: reflect a coord offset for kaleidoscope-style folds.
Chain with Dot Product to measure alignment of the bounce.

node:refract.title: Refract
node:refract.tagline: Bends an incident ray through a surface (IOR ratio).
node:refract.description: Refracts I through N using index ratio eta. Leave eta unwired to use the Eta (IOR) knob; total internal reflection returns zero.

inputs.name: I
inputs.description: Incident direction (entering surface). Often Normalize(UV) or view direction.

inputs.name: N
inputs.description: Surface normal (normalized). Often from Normal Mapping or Constant Vec2.

inputs.name: eta
inputs.description: Ratio n1/n2 (e.g. 0.75 for air→glass). Connect Constant Float or Divide.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Refracted direction. Connect to Normalize, Dot Product, or Lighting Shading.

node:refract.hook: Connect Normalize(incident) to I, surface normal to N, and set Eta (IOR) for glass-like bend.

parameters.name: Eta (IOR)
parameters.description: Fallback index ratio when eta is unconnected. Below 1 bends toward the normal; above 1 bends away (glass-like).

examples: Eta ≈ 0.92 on a vec2 normal for a subtle glass displacement direction.
Refract a UV offset for prism-style coordinate bending.
Pair with Reflect to compare bounce vs bend on the same normal.
node:refract.advanced: IOR is the ratio of indices (e.g. air to glass). At grazing angles the result can vanish—that is total internal reflection.

node:blend.title: Blend
node:blend.tagline: Blend two values with Photoshop-style modes — float, vec2, vec3, or vec4 from your wires
node:blend.description: Takes Background and Blend inputs whose type is inferred from connections (defaults to float when unwired). Each component uses the selected blend mode (Normal through Exclusion). Opacity mixes the blended result toward Background.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: Background layer. Unwired defaults to typed zero.

inputs.name: blend
inputs.description: Blend layer combined onto Background with the selected mode.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Blended result (same arity as resolved inputs).

examples: Wire two float masks for scalar blending before Final Output.
Chain vec4 color pipelines; use Alpha Lerp for layer-style RGBA.
Pick Overlay or Soft Light and lower Opacity for photo-style tints.
node:blend.advanced: For vec4 only, Alpha chooses Lerp (RGB modes + alpha interpolated) or Blend (apply the mode to alpha as well). Not Porter–Duff compositing; linear channel math in the shader working space. Mode 0=Normal, 1=Multiply, …, 11=Exclusion. vec4 Alpha Lerp matches former Blend; float-only graphs match former Blend.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Switches the visual style or algorithm variant.

parameters.name: Opacity
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

parameters.name: Alpha
parameters.description: Whole-number control for Alpha. Higher values usually increase count or steps.

node:oklch-color-map.title: Color Map
node:oklch-color-map.tagline: Map a 0–1 value to RGB through OKLCH with smooth or stepped bands, per-channel Bézier curves, and optional Bayer dither
node:oklch-color-map.description: Converts a float value (0–1) to an RGB color in OKLCH (perceptual lightness, chroma, hue). Smooth mode eases the input through independent L/C/H cubic Bézier curves between start and end colors.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The input value (0–1) to map to a color

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The resulting RGB color converted from OKLCH

examples: Use Smooth for continuous gradients; Stepped for posterized bands or stylized palettes.
Feed Noise or patterns into Value; tune L/C/H curves to shape how the ramp maps through OKLCH.
In Stepped mode, raise Dither Strength to soften band edges without extra nodes.
node:oklch-color-map.advanced: Stepped mode quantizes the input into discrete bands (Stops) with adjustable transition width; optional built-in Bayer dither reduces banding. Colors and curves are edited in the panel; only the scalar Value input is exposed on the graph. Mode Smooth (0) vs Stepped (1). Stepped mode uses Stops and Transition Width; Dither Strength applies screen-space Bayer when > 0. Reverse hue controls hue interpolation direction around the OKLCH wheel.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Switches the visual style or algorithm variant.

parameters.name: Start Light
parameters.description: Adjusts Start Light between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Start Chroma
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

parameters.name: Start Hue
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

parameters.name: End Light
parameters.description: Adjusts End Light between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: End Chroma
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

parameters.name: End Hue
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

parameters.name: Swap Colors
parameters.description: Adjusts color appearance on screen; pair with the color swatch when shown.

parameters.name: lCurveX1
parameters.description: Adjusts lCurveX1 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: lCurveY1
parameters.description: Adjusts lCurveY1 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: lCurveX2
parameters.description: Adjusts lCurveX2 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: lCurveY2
parameters.description: Adjusts lCurveY2 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: cCurveX1
parameters.description: Adjusts cCurveX1 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: cCurveY1
parameters.description: Adjusts cCurveY1 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: cCurveX2
parameters.description: Adjusts cCurveX2 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: cCurveY2
parameters.description: Adjusts cCurveY2 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: hCurveX1
parameters.description: Adjusts hCurveX1 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: hCurveY1
parameters.description: Adjusts hCurveY1 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: hCurveX2
parameters.description: Adjusts hCurveX2 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: hCurveY2
parameters.description: Adjusts hCurveY2 between 0 and 1; higher values usually intensify the look.

node:glow-bloom.title: Glow
node:glow-bloom.tagline: Bloom from bright passes: halo around highlights (full blur on WebGPU; fast preview elsewhere)
node:glow-bloom.description: WebGPU path: threshold masked bright pixels, blur them wide, then add back—a real-ish bloom spill. WebGL preview: bright-pass on Rec.709 luminance preserves hue, then Strength × a Radius-aware spread boost approximates softer bloom until multipass kicks in.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Input color to glow. Connect vec4 from Mix, Blend, OKLCH color-map nodes, or other color chains here.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The color with glow and bloom effects applied

examples: Chain: UV → Noise → Output → Glow → Output for a glowing grayscale pattern.
Add glow after Mix or Blend to make bright blended areas bloom.
Feed Glow output into Edge Detection or Color Grading for stylized looks.
node:glow-bloom.advanced: Connect vec4 chains into Color toward Final Output or downstream grade. WebGPU consumes Radius in the Gaussian separable blur pass; preview paths lean on Threshold/Intensity/Strength with Radius as spread hint.
node:glow-bloom.hook: Connect bright color → Glow → Final Output to bloom highlights.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: Higher keeps only stronger regions; lower includes more of the input.

parameters.name: Intensity
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Larger values enlarge the feature; smaller values make it finer or tighter.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

node:blur.title: Blur
node:blur.tagline: Gaussian / directional / radial separable blur (WebGPU)—WebGL previews with weighted luminance soften
node:blur.description: Softens color with Gaussian, directional, or radial blur. On WebGPU, … → Blur → Final Output uses a real separable pass; inline chains (Mix, Glow) use a fast preview approximation like WebGL.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Scene or graded color you want softened. Typical: … → Output → Blur → Final Output.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Blurred RGB (Gaussian on WebGPU when directly before Final Output). Alpha preserved where supported.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: Blur mix: raise this to reveal blur. Matches the WebGPU pass blend toward blurred output—when Amount is 0 you see no blur even if Radius is high.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: How strong the blur is once Amount > 0. On WebGPU the kernel spread grows with Radius (pixels) times Amount.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Gaussian blur in all directions, Directional streak along Angle, or Radial blur outward from radial center.

examples: Soften procedural noise before output: Noise → Output → Blur (Gaussian) → Final Output on WebGPU for true neighbor blur.
Directional mode + Direction for horizontal film streak or motion-blur vibes; dial Amount then Radius.
Radial mode: set Center slightly off-axis for asymmetric smear toward an edge focal point.
Chain Blur into Mix or Glow when you want a lighter inline blur—expect a softer preview match until you reconnect before Final Output.
node:blur.advanced: Blend, Mix, Glow) and WebGPU uses the same single-pass approximation as the WebGL preview so previews stay responsive. WebGL cannot sample neighborhoods: Amount turns the effect on/off (gates how much softened luminance mixes in), Radius scales blur strength once Amount is raised, Mode picks Gaussian, Directional, or Radial, and Direction / radial center tweak the approximation so it tracks the eventual WebGPU blur. Coordinate note (radial): Center axes use the WGSL radial mapping UV focal = (0.5, 0.5) + 0.5 × (Center X, Center Y) inside 0–1 UV—roughly ±1 spans the plane from center toward edges; widen the Range if you deliberately overshoot.
node:blur.hook: Chain … → Output → Blur → Final Output on WebGPU for true neighbor blur.

node:edge-detection.title: Edge Detection
node:edge-detection.tagline: Threshold ridge on luminance—not full Sobel / neighbor convolution
node:edge-detection.description: Builds an edge mask from distance of Rec.709 luminance to Threshold, smoothed by Width, then mixes toward Intensity with Strength. Output preserves saturation by scaling RGB with the ridge factor.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The input color to detect edges in

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The color with edge detection effects applied

node:edge-detection.advanced: Useful for illustrative outlines where you want perceptual breaks, not convolution-accurate image edges.
node:edge-detection.hook: Connect pattern color → Edge Detection → Mix for outline overlays.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: Higher keeps only stronger regions; lower includes more of the input.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Larger values enlarge the feature; smaller values make it finer or tighter.

parameters.name: Intensity
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

examples: Place Edge Detection late in the chain: pattern → Output → Edge Detection → Final Output.
Dial Amount/Strength first, then Radius or Mode for the look you want.

node:chromatic-aberration.title: Chromatic Aberration
node:chromatic-aberration.tagline: Radial lens-style RGB tilt from center—Direction rotates the fringe axis
node:chromatic-aberration.description: Screenspace modulation (no per-channel UV resampling): from each pixel, boosts/cuts R/B along a radial vector projected onto Direction (degrees).

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The input color to apply chromatic aberration to

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The color with RGB channel separation applied
