node:chromatic-aberration.advanced: Strength scales separation, Falloff damps farther from center, center offsets sit in normalized screen space—good for prismy edges or subtle lens quirks. Differs from RGB Separation, which biases channels with planar dot offsets.

parameters.name: Direction
parameters.description: Rotates or shifts the pattern; try small changes first for subtle motion.

parameters.name: Falloff
parameters.description: Controls how quickly the effect fades with distance from center or source.

parameters.name: Center X
parameters.description: Moves the focal point across the canvas in normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: Center Y
parameters.description: Moves the focal point across the canvas in normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: Raise to strengthen the effect; lower to fade or soften it.

examples: Place Chromatic Aberration late in the chain: pattern → Output → Chromatic Aberration → Final Output.
Dial Amount/Strength first, then Radius or Mode for the look you want.

node:cellular-slip.title: Cellular Slip
node:cellular-slip.tagline: Voronoi glass-plate UV warp—each cell slides and rotates on its own
node:cellular-slip.description: Partitions UV into Voronoi cells and displaces each cell independently (slide + rotation) with optional edge lock so seams stay soft or crisp. Chain UV Coords → Cellular Slip → Noise to see shifting tiles—not rectangular Block Glitch jumps or the float Cells pattern.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV coordinates to warp (aspect-correct p from UV Coords is typical).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Cell-slipped UV for downstream sampling or further Distort nodes.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Voronoi cell density; higher = more, smaller cells.

parameters.name: Jitter
parameters.description: Randomizes seed positions; 0 = regular grid, 1 = organic cells.

parameters.name: Slip
parameters.description: Per-cell translation amount; animate or audio-drive for motion.

parameters.name: Rotate
parameters.description: Per-cell rotation in degrees (hash-driven per cell).

parameters.name: Edge
parameters.description: Softness width at cell borders when Lock is on.

parameters.name: Lock
parameters.description: When on, blends slipped UV back toward input near cell edges.

parameters.name: Seed
parameters.description: Offsets cell IDs for different plate layouts.

parameters.name: Step Hz
parameters.description: Quantizes seed stepping to time for stuttered plate updates.

parameters.name: Blend
parameters.description: Mix between input UV and warped UV (0 = passthrough, 1 = full slip).

examples: UV → Cellular Slip → Noise: raise Scale and Slip for sliding glass plates over a texture field.
Enable Lock with small Edge for soft seams; disable Lock for hard cell motion.
Drive Slip or Rotate from audio bands for beat-reactive plate shifts.
node:cellular-slip.advanced: Use Blend to mix back toward the input UV. Per-cell motion uses hashed offsets—not shared global translation like Displace. Distinct from Cells (float F1/F2 pattern) and Block Glitch (rectangular UV jumps).

node:circle-inversion.title: Circle Inversion
node:circle-inversion.tagline: Iterative multi-circle UV inversion with layout presets
node:circle-inversion.description: Applies one or more circle inversions per iteration around preset centers (triangle, chain, flower, random), with soft boundaries and global rotation/scale. Outputs vec2 UV for chaining—not Spotlight color accumulation and not KIFS SDF (signed distance field) 3D folds.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV to invert (typically from UV Coords or an upstream Distort).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Inversion-warped UV coordinates.

parameters.name: Layout
parameters.description: Preset arrangement of inversion circle centers.

parameters.name: Circles
parameters.description: How many circles participate per iteration (up to four).

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Inversion circle radius in UV space.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: How strongly each inversion pulls coordinates (0–1).

parameters.name: Iterations
parameters.description: Repeat the multi-circle inversion pass.

parameters.name: Soft
parameters.description: Soft boundary width so inversions fade in smoothly.

parameters.name: Rotation
parameters.description: Global rotation applied after each circle step.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Scales preset center positions.

parameters.name: Clamp
parameters.description: Max UV length after warp; prevents runaway coordinates.

parameters.name: Blend
parameters.description: Mix input UV with inverted UV.

examples: Start with Layout Triangle, Circles 3, Iterations 2, Blend ~0.7 for bubble-like UV folds before Noise.
Lower Strength and raise Soft for gentler inversions; use Clamp if previews blow out.
Compare with Spotlight: same inversion idea but Spotlight outputs accumulated color, not UV.
node:circle-inversion.advanced: Keep Blend below 1 for safer previews; strength and radius affect how aggressively space inverts. Singularities near circle boundaries are softened and clamped; conservative defaults avoid poles on the unit boundary. Not a migration path from legacy Bulge/Fisheye nodes.

node:crease-fold.title: Crease Fold
node:crease-fold.tagline: Soft hinged mirror fold across a moving crease line—optional repeat grid
node:crease-fold.description: Reflects/compresses UV across a crease defined by Angle and Offset (plus Phase), with softness and optional repeating bands. Linear hinge fold—not radial Kaleidoscope symmetry. Wire UV Coords → Crease Fold → Noise; use Blend to dial effect strength.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV coordinates to fold.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Folded UV coordinates.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Crease line orientation in degrees.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Slides the crease along its normal (two-sided knob).

parameters.name: Fold
parameters.description: Fold amount; 0 = no mirror, 1 = full reflection mix.

parameters.name: Soft
parameters.description: Softens the crease transition.

parameters.name: Repeat
parameters.description: Spacing for repeated crease bands; 0 = single crease.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: Number of repeat folds to apply.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Animatable offset along the crease normal.

parameters.name: Blend
parameters.description: Mix between input and folded UV.

examples: Animate Phase or Offset for a traveling crease; add Repeat for accordion stripes.
Keep Soft > 0 when Fold is high to avoid harsh seams.
Pair with Kaleidoscope only when you want both linear folds and radial mirrors—order matters.
node:crease-fold.advanced: Repeat alternates fold direction per band (even/odd). Distinct from KIFS SDF (signed distance field) iterated 3D folds used in raymarching.

node:mobius-portal.title: Möbius Portal
node:mobius-portal.tagline: Conformal disk automorphism—off-center pole bends UV through a portal
node:mobius-portal.description: Maps aspect-correct UV with a Möbius transform on the disk: move Center and Pole to bend space so straight lines become circles—different from symmetric Radial Warp bulge. Pole limit keeps the pole inside the disk; Edge soft fades the map near the boundary.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV entering the portal (UV Coords or upstream Distort).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Portal-warped UV.

parameters.name: Center X
parameters.description: Disk map center X (coords UI).

parameters.name: Center Y
parameters.description: Disk map center Y (coords UI).

parameters.name: Pole X
parameters.description: Möbius pole X; drives conformal bend direction.

parameters.name: Pole Y
parameters.description: Adjusts Pole Y between -2 and 2; higher values usually intensify the look.

parameters.name: Pole limit
parameters.description: Scales pole vector; keeps pole inside unit disk.

parameters.name: Rotation
parameters.description: Post-map rotation in degrees.

parameters.name: Zoom
parameters.description: Scales coordinates before the map.

parameters.name: Edge soft
parameters.description: Fades warp near disk edge.

parameters.name: Blend
parameters.description: Mix input UV with portal UV.

examples: UV → Kaleidoscope → Möbius Portal → Noise for symmetric segments bent through a portal.
Wire Path Drive X/Y into Pole X/Y for wandering portal centers.
Lower Blend (~0.5) while tuning pole; raise Edge soft if rim artifacts appear.
node:mobius-portal.advanced: Singularities are clamped—avoid pole on the rim with defaults. Rational map denominator is epsilon-clamped; output length is capped. Conformal on the disk—not a fisheye lens (Radial Warp Fisheye mode).

node:wake-smear.title: Wake Smear
node:wake-smear.tagline: Capsule-trail UV drag along preset paths—datamosh-like smear without frame history
node:wake-smear.description: Multiple emitters follow Path presets (line, orbit, figure-8, drift); each leaves a capsule-shaped UV drag trail with decay, curl, and optional Quantize stepping. Procedural motion-vector smear—no ping-pong buffers or video optical flow.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV to drag along emitter trails.

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Smear-warped UV.

parameters.name: Emitters
parameters.description: Number of simultaneous trail emitters (up to six).

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Emitter motion preset: Line, Orbit, Figure-8, or Drift.

parameters.name: Speed
parameters.description: How fast emitters move along the path.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: Trail extent along the path (head–tail separation).

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Perpendicular falloff of the capsule influence.

parameters.name: Drag
parameters.description: UV pull strength along the trail tangent.

parameters.name: Curl
parameters.description: Adds perpendicular swirl along the trail (two-sided).

parameters.name: Decay
parameters.description: How quickly drag fades toward the tail.

parameters.name: Quantize
parameters.description: Step time for stuttered smear updates (Hz).

parameters.name: Blend
parameters.description: Mix input UV with smeared UV.

examples: Path Orbit + Speed ~0.5 + Drag ~0.3: circular smear wakes over Noise.
Raise Quantize Hz for stepped datamosh stutter; add Curl for swirly trails.
Use Path Drive to offset emitter paths indirectly via downstream center params on other nodes, or animate Speed/Drag from audio.
node:wake-smear.advanced: Chain after UV Coords; reduce Blend for subtle trails. No interframe feedback—pure procedural trails. Distinct from Block Glitch rectangular jumps and continuous Turbulence noise warp.

node:color-gradient.title: Color Gradient
node:color-gradient.tagline: Spatial 3-stop OKLCH ramp multiplied by Value — zero strength stays black
node:color-gradient.description: Builds an RGB color from a 3-stop OKLCH (perceptual lightness, chroma, hue) ramp along Position (radial or linear in screen space). Value scales how much of that color appears: at 0 the output is black (no additive base).

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Strength mask (0–1). Low values darken toward black after the spatial ramp is computed.

inputs.name: position
inputs.description: Coordinates for the spatial ramp (UV, screen, or custom vec2).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: RGB color from the ramp × value mask.

examples: UV → Position, Noise → Value, Color Gradient → Final Output for a sky-like ramp with dark noise valleys.
Use Radial for orbs and vignette color; Linear for horizontal or angled sweeps.
Raise Gain or lower Softness on Value to punch up highlights; combine with Mix for layered tints.
node:color-gradient.advanced: Tune stops with the panel pickers, radial center/radius or linear angle, and Gain / Power / Softness on Value. For masks without color, use Gradient; for Bézier curves and stepped bands, use Color Map. Hue interpolates on the shortest OKLCH path between stops. Three line families at 0°, 60°, 120°; Edge / Fill mix linearly blends the edge mask with the alternating cell parity. Output is lit grayscale shading (depth factor plus optional glow term, multiplied by lighting), not a raw signed distance. Where the ray misses geometry the output stays at zero; the glow term is evaluated only on a surface hit. Lighting supports directional or point light with optional shadows. Specular group: enable Cook-Torrance (GGX + Fresnel) for PBR-style specular; Roughness and F0 control the look. Optional Ray origin and Ray direction: when connected (e.g. from Orbit Camera), the node uses that camera; when unconnected, Ro X/Y/Z under Camera set the built-in ray origin and UV drives the default perspective ray direction. When Ray origin / Ray direction inputs are unconnected, Ro X/Y/Z (Camera section) set the built-in ray origin and UV builds a perspective ray direction. For a shared rig across multiple 3D nodes, connect one Orbit Camera or Look-at Camera to all. SDF combination order (if you later combine with other SDFs) affects which shape is in front.

node:metaballs.title: Metaballs
node:metaballs.tagline: 3D raymarched metaballs: soft blobs that blend where their fields overlap
node:metaballs.description: Renders 3D metaballs using raymarching. Metaballs are soft blobs whose influence fields are summed; the visible surface is where the combined field exceeds a threshold. Blob count (2–6), radius, threshold, and orbit radius control the shape; blobs orbit around the scene center.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV coordinates to raymarch from (e.g. from UV Coords)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Surface and glow value (float); use with Final Output or Mix

examples: Connect UV to in; output to Output or Mix for 3D metaballs (soft blobs that merge where fields overlap).
Use with Orbit Camera or built-in orbit; adjust blob count, radius, threshold, and orbit radius for shape and motion.
Feed output to Output or Mix for shading; layer with Primitives or Raymarch Sphere for mixed 3D scenes.
node:metaballs.advanced: Use Position to move the group, Animation for orbit speed, and Appearance for raymarch steps and glow. Connect UV to in and wire out to Final Output or Mix for shading. Metaball surface is where the sum of blob influence fields exceeds a threshold; blobs orbit the scene center. More blobs (2–6) and higher raymarch steps improve quality at higher cost.
node:metaballs.hook: Connect UV → Metaballs → Output for soft blob merges.

node:sky-dome.title: Skydome
node:sky-dome.tagline: Procedural sky dome with zenith/horizon gradient, optional sun disc, and a virtual camera (FOV, yaw, pitch, roll)
node:sky-dome.description: Outputs a procedural sky as vec4 (RGBA) suitable for use behind raymarched 3D scenes. Sky color is blended from horizon to zenith; an optional sun disc is added when the view ray is close to the sun direction.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: UV coordinates to compute sky ray direction (e.g. from UV Coords)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Sky color (RGB) and alpha 1.0

examples: Connect UV to in; output to Mix or Final Output as background behind raymarched 3D (e.g. Primitives, Raymarch Sphere, SDF Raymarch).
Click the Sky swatches to open the OKLCH color picker (or tweak L/C/H knobs directly); add a sun disc with Sun direction and radius for a full sky look.

Use the View group to frame the sky: FOV widens or narrows the dome, the Yaw/Pitch pad pans and tilts the virtual camera, and Roll cants the horizon — useful for matching the camera of a 3D scene mixed underneath.
Use as the second input to Mix with 3D node output (e.g. box-torus-sdf) so the sky shows where the ray misses geometry.
node:sky-dome.advanced: Use Sky group to set zenith and horizon as OKLCH colors (click the swatches for the picker, or edit L/C/H directly) and horizon softness; Sun group sets direction (Dir X/Y/Z), radius (radians), and intensity; View group sets the virtual camera — FOV (degrees), yaw/pitch (XY pad: pan and tilt), and roll. Connect UV (e.g. from UV Coords) to in; connect out to mix, final output, or Blend / Blend. Sky ray direction is derived from UV with an adjustable virtual camera. The default FOV of 90° reproduces the legacy fixed projection (uv*2-1, -1.0); shrinking FOV zooms in, widening it shows more of the dome. Yaw rotates around vertical, pitch tilts around horizontal, and roll rotates around the forward axis (applied as roll → pitch → yaw). Horizon softness widens the horizon→zenith blend band. Sun disc is drawn when the view ray is close to the sun direction; intensity and radius (radians) control brightness and size. Colors are stored in OKLCH for perceptually uniform editing and tween better than raw RGB.

node:compare.title: Compare
node:compare.tagline: Compare: Compares two values and outputs 0.0 or 1.0
node:compare.description: Compares two input values using a selected comparison operation and outputs 1.0 if the condition is true, 0.0 otherwise. The available operations include equal (==), not equal (!=), less than (<), less than or equal (<=), greater than (>), and greater than or equal (>=).

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: The first value to compare

inputs.name: b

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: 1.0 if the comparison is true, 0.0 otherwise

examples: Compare Noise or Distance to a threshold (e.g. equal, greater) for binary masks.
Use output as condition for Select to pick one of two values.
Drive Mix factor or gradient mask from comparison (1.0 or 0.0).
Feed Mask BW, Mask UV, or Mask Color mask inputs for sharp region splits (1.0 or 0.0).
node:compare.advanced: This is essential for creating conditional logic, thresholds, and binary masks based on value comparisons. The output can be used to drive other nodes or create selective effects. Output is 1.0 when condition true, 0.0 otherwise. For smooth transitions use Smoothstep; for hard edges use Step.

node:select.title: Select
node:select.tagline: Select: Selects between two values based on condition
node:select.description: Selects between two input values based on a condition. If the condition is greater than 0.5, it returns the true value; otherwise, it returns the false value. Port order is If false, If true, then Condition (bottom).

inputs.name: trueValue

outputs.name: out

examples: Wire Compare or Step into Condition for hard branching between two floats or colors.
Choose between two Output outputs for a simple A/B look.
Use panel If true / If false when ports are unwired; connect If true / If false to override with graph values.
node:select.advanced: When the condition port is unwired, the Condition control on the node supplies the value—typically 0.0–1.0, where values above 0.5 count as true. The If true and If false branches are wired-only (no duplicate body controls). Useful for conditional routing, switching inputs, or if-else style logic. Condition treats values above 0.5 as true. For grayscale masks near 0.5, small changes can flip the branch—use Smoothstep or clamp if you need stability.

parameters.name: Condition
parameters.description: Turns this section of the effect on or off.

node:mask-composite-float.title: Mask BW
node:mask-composite-float.tagline: Composites foreground over background using a float mask; dark areas show background, bright areas show foreground.
node:mask-composite-float.description: Blends two float values (background and foreground) using a mask. Where the mask is dark (low values), the background appears; where it is bright (high values), the foreground appears. Port order matches mix(background, foreground, mask): Background, then Mask, then Foreground.

inputs.name: bg
inputs.description: Background value (shown where mask is dark)

inputs.name: mask
inputs.description: Mask value 0–1: dark = bg, bright = fg

inputs.name: fg
inputs.description: Foreground value (shown where mask is bright)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Result of mixing bg and fg by mask

parameters.name: Background
parameters.description: Used for bg when nothing is connected. This value appears where the mask is dark (0); set to 0 for black, 1 for white in grayscale.

parameters.name: Mask
parameters.description: Default mask value when mask input is unconnected. 0 = show background everywhere; 1 = show foreground; in between = blend.

parameters.name: Foreground
parameters.description: Used for fg when nothing is connected. This value appears where the mask is bright (1); set to control the bright areas of the result.

parameters.name: Invert
parameters.description: When on, the mix uses (1 − mask) so bright and dark regions swap roles relative to background vs foreground.

node:mask-composite-float.advanced: Connect a float mask (e.g. from Noise, Step, or Smoothstep) to the mask input, and set or connect the background and foreground values. Turn on Invert to swap which mask values favor background vs foreground (uses 1 − mask as the mix weight). Useful for masking patterns, blending values, or driving mix factors.

Use Mask BW to pick between two colors or vectors without duplicating upstream nodes.

parameters.name: Invert

Use Invert when the mask should favor background coordinates in bright regions.

Turn on Invert to swap which mask values favor background vs foreground (uses 1 − mask as the mix weight). Replaces splitting UV, masking each axis with Mask BW, and combining again.

node:mask-composite-vec3.title: Mask Color
node:mask-composite-vec3.tagline: Composites colored foreground over colored background using a float mask.

inputs.description: Foreground color (shown where mask is bright)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Result color from mixing bg and fg by mask

parameters.description: Default mask value when mask input is unconnected. 0 = show background color everywhere; 1 = show foreground; in between = blend between the two colors.

parameters.name: Invert
parameters.description: When on, the mix uses (1 − mask) so bright and dark regions swap roles relative to background vs foreground.

node:mask-composite-vec3.advanced: Connect Mix, OKLCH (perceptual lightness, chroma, hue) color-map nodes, or other vec3 sources to bg and fg, and a float mask to the mask input. Turn on Invert to swap which mask values favor background vs foreground (uses 1 − mask as the mix weight). Ideal for combining two color layers or applying masks to colored results.
examples: Drive Condition from Compare or a pattern threshold, then route true/false paths.
Use Mask Color to pick between two colors or vectors without duplicating upstream nodes.

node:one-minus.title: One Minus
node:one-minus.tagline: One Minus: Subtracts input from 1.0 (invert for 0-1 range)
node:one-minus.description: Subtracts the input value from 1.0, effectively inverting values in the 0-1 range. When the input is 0.0, the output is 1.0; when the input is 1.0, the output is 0.0. This is commonly used for inverting masks, flipping gradients, or creating inverse relationships.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to invert (subtract from 1.0)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The inverted value (1.0 - input)

node:one-minus.advanced: The operation is equivalent to (1.0 - input) and is a fundamental utility for many shader operations that require inverted values.

node:negate.title: Negate
node:negate.tagline: Use this to negate (flip sign) of a value, converting positive to negative and vice versa
node:negate.description: Negates the input value by multiplying it by -1.0, effectively flipping its sign. Positive values become negative, and negative values become positive. Zero remains zero. This is useful for reversing directions, inverting offsets, or creating mirror effects.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to negate

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The negated value (-input)

examples: Negate(offset) to reverse direction of Translate or displacement.
Flip sign of Sine or a difference for mirrored motion or symmetry.

node:negate.advanced: The operation is equivalent to (-input) and is a fundamental utility for many mathematical operations.

node:reciprocal.title: Reciprocal
node:reciprocal.description: Calculates the reciprocal of the input value by dividing 1.0 by the input. The reciprocal of a number is its multiplicative inverse, so multiplying a value by its reciprocal equals 1.0.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to calculate the reciprocal of (must not be zero)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The reciprocal value (1.0 / input)

examples: Reciprocal(Length or Distance) for 1/r falloff (avoid zero input).
Multiply by Reciprocal instead of Divide when same divisor is reused.
Invert a scale factor (e.g. 1/period for frequency).
node:reciprocal.advanced: This is useful for inverting scales, converting rates to periods, or performing division when you need to multiply by the inverse. Be careful with values near zero, as the reciprocal approaches infinity. Input must not be zero; use Max(input, small) or branch to avoid division by zero.

node:clamp-01.title: Clamp 01
node:clamp-01.tagline: Use this to clamp values to the 0.0-1.0 range, ensuring they stay within valid bounds
node:clamp-01.description: Clamps the input value to the range 0.0 to 1.0. Values below 0.0 become 0.0, values above 1.0 become 1.0, and values within the range remain unchanged. This is a specialized version of the clamp node with fixed bounds, commonly used in shader programming.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to clamp to 0.0-1.0 range

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The clamped value (between 0.0 and 1.0)

examples: Clamp Sine or Noise to 0–1 before using as mask or Mix factor.
Ensure a value is in valid range for Output or blend inputs.
Same as Saturate; use when you want explicit 0–1 bounds.
node:clamp-01.advanced: It's equivalent to clamp(input, 0.0, 1.0) and is essential for ensuring values stay within normalized ranges, particularly for colors, masks, and blend factors.

node:saturate.title: Saturate
node:saturate.tagline: Same as Clamp 01, a common shader programming term for clamping to 0-1 range
node:saturate.description: Saturates the input value by clamping it to the 0.0-1.0 range. This is identical to the Clamp 01 node but uses the common shader programming term 'saturate'.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to saturate (clamp to 0.0-1.0)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The saturated value (clamped between 0.0 and 1.0)

examples: Saturate after Add or Multiply to keep result in 0–1 for masks or colors.
Identical to Clamp 01; use for shader-style naming in 0–1 clamping.
Apply to Dot Product or signed value before Mix for safe blend factor.
node:saturate.advanced: The function ensures values stay within the normalized range, which is essential for color channels, blend factors, and many shader operations. Values below 0.0 become 0.0, values above 1.0 become 1.0, and values within range remain unchanged.

node:sign.title: Sign
node:sign.tagline: Sign: Returns sign of value (-1.0, 0.0, or 1.0)
node:sign.description: Returns the sign of the input value: -1.0 for negative values, 0.0 for zero, and 1.0 for positive values. This is useful for determining direction, creating conditional logic based on sign, or extracting the sign component of a value.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to get the sign of

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The sign value (-1.0, 0.0, or 1.0)

examples: Sign(offset or direction) to get -1, 0, or 1 for branching or flip.
Use with Multiply to apply direction without magnitude.
Detect positive/negative for conditional logic or Select-style routing.
node:sign.advanced: The sign function is commonly used in mathematical operations where you need to know whether a value is positive or negative without caring about its magnitude.

node:round.title: Round
node:round.description: Rounds the input value to the nearest integer. Values exactly halfway between integers round to the nearest even integer (banker's rounding). This is useful for quantizing values, creating discrete steps, or converting continuous values to integer-like values.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to round to the nearest integer

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The rounded value (nearest integer)

Quantize a 0–1 value for stepped Output or banding effects.
Banker's rounding (half rounds to even); use Floor/Ceil for deterministic direction.
node:round.advanced: Rounding is commonly used for pixel-perfect effects, grid snapping, or creating stepped animations.

node:truncate.title: Truncate
node:truncate.tagline: Use this to truncate (remove fractional part) of a value, rounding towards zero
node:truncate.description: Truncates the input value by removing its fractional part, effectively rounding towards zero. Positive values are rounded down, and negative values are rounded up (towards zero). This is different from floor, which always rounds down.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The value to truncate (remove fractional part)

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The truncated value (fractional part removed)

examples: Truncate(Time or value) to drop fractional part (round toward zero).
Same as Floor for positive values; differs for negative (truncate goes toward zero).
Get integer part of a float for indexing or discrete bands.
node:truncate.advanced: Truncation is useful for creating discrete values, quantizing, or extracting the integer component of a number. The result is always closer to zero than the input.

node:lerp.title: Lerp

node:lerp.description: Performs linear interpolation (lerp) between two values, which is identical to the Mix node. When the blend factor (t) is 0.0, it returns the first value (a). When t is 1.0, it returns the second value (b). Values in between are linearly interpolated.

node:bayer-dither.title: Bayer Dither
node:bayer-dither.tagline: Bayer Dither: Applies Bayer dithering to a float value using fragment coordinates
node:bayer-dither.description: Applies Bayer dithering to a float value using fragment coordinates to create an ordered dither pattern. Bayer dithering uses a threshold matrix to add controlled noise that breaks up banding artifacts in gradients and color transitions.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The input value to apply dithering to

inputs.name: fragCoord
inputs.description: Fragment coordinates for dithering pattern calculation

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Screen resolution for dithering calculations

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The dithered value with Bayer pattern applied

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: Scales the Bayer noise amplitude before clamping onto the incoming float lane.

parameters.name: Pixel Size
parameters.description: Divisor applied to centered fragment coordinates before Bayer indexing—pixels per Bayer macro-cell across the framebuffer (same units as `fragCoord`; raise it to enlarge the checker on screen).

node:bayer-dither.advanced: The dithering strength and pixel size can be configured to control the intensity and scale of the dither pattern. This is particularly useful for reducing color banding in gradients, especially when working with limited color depth or when creating retro/vintage aesthetics that benefit from dithering artifacts.

node:tone-mapping.title: Tone Mapping
node:tone-mapping.tagline: Exposure × contrast pivot × saturation clamped to linear 0–1
node:tone-mapping.description: Exposure multiplies RGB, Contrast pivots mid-gray at 0.5, Saturation lerps RGB toward luminance weighted like Rec.709. Output is clamped to linear 0–1 (`clamp`), so wildly HDR upstream values flatten—pair with deliberate scaling or earlier OKLCH (perceptual lightness, chroma, hue)/grade nodes if you routinely excee

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The input RGB color to apply tone mapping to

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: The tone-mapped color with exposure, contrast, and saturation adjustments

examples: Chain Color Grading → Tone Mapping → Output to adjust exposure and contrast before display.
Use after Glow or post-process nodes to tame highlights and set final saturation.
Place near the end of the pipeline; combine with Color Grading for full control over shadows, midtones, and highlights.
node:tone-mapping.advanced: d 1.0 intentionally. Exposure scales luminance; contrast centers around 0.5 and compresses or expands range; saturation mixes color with its luminance. Order matters: tone mapping after color grading gives a final trim, before grading affects the curve input.

parameters.name: Exposure
parameters.description: Adjusts Exposure between 0 and 5; higher values usually intensify the look.

node:final-output.title: Output
node:final-output.tagline: This is where your image comes from. Connect a color—or a float (promoted to vec3)—here to see it on screen.
node:final-output.hook: Wire your final color (or a float from Noise) into in to see it in preview.
node:final-output.description: End of the graph: whatever you connect to in appears in preview. Accepts vec3 color; floats (e.g. from Noise) show as grayscale. Every graph needs exactly one Output node.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: The color to show on screen. Connect a float (grayscale via vec3 promotion) or vec3 from Mix, Blend, Tone Mapping, or other color nodes.

node:radial-pulse.title: Radial Pulse
node:radial-pulse.tagline: Expanding circular wavefronts from a center—distinct from repeating Rings.
node:radial-pulse.description: Outputs an expanding ring from Center. Wire Position (or UV) to in; connect out to Mix or a color ramp. Preview respawns on Loop interval when Drive has no audio; wire Drive for beat-synced pulses.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Sample position (typically UV or planar coordinates).

outputs.name: out
outputs.description: Ring intensity 0–1 at each pixel.
